patients.summary: 51-year-old woman with Crohn's disease, short bowel syndrome and long-term home TPN, recurrent severe depression and anxiety, who joined in 2020. Her course includes temporal lobe epilepsy, a right superior gluteal nerve palsy, acalculous cholecystitis with cholecystectomy, a provoked PE after knee arthroscopy, psychotic depression in 2024, and central pontine myelinolysis after hyponatremia correction in 2025 with partial recovery.

- Allergy list: NSAIDs, gabapentin (both listed as ineffective / GI intolerance).

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
NEW PATIENT — establishing care

45F transferring from prior PCP (records reviewed, see 7/10 scan). Came alone.

HPI: Complicated GI history. Crohn's of the small bowel, multiple resections, now short bowel and on home TPN 12 h every night through a tunneled line. TPN and line are run by her GI/intestinal rehab team and the home infusion company; she wants us for "everything else." GI also gives her vedolizumab infusions every 8 weeks for the Crohn's; no flares in years.

Main concern today is mood. Since roughly April she's felt flat and sad, stopped doing the things she likes, can't focus to read or follow a show, sleeping badly. Thinks she's lost weight. Feels she's "no good to anybody." Has been through this twice before (late 20s, mid-30s), both times needed medication. Has an outside psychiatrist who prescribes sertraline and bupropion; last saw them in the spring, next appt not until the fall. Takes alprazolam 0.25 now and then for anxiety, sometimes 2 at night. Diphenhydramine most nights to sleep. No thoughts of harming herself.

Back pain: years of low back pain, worse some weeks than others. NSAIDs upset her stomach and did nothing, gabapentin did nothing, PT "didn't do anything."

PMH: Crohn's/short bowel/TPN as above; recurrent major depression; generalized anxiety; chronic low back pain.
PSH: several small bowel resections; tunneled central venous catheter for TPN.
Meds: sertraline 100 daily, bupropion XL 150 qAM, alprazolam 0.25 prn, diphenhydramine 25 qhs prn, norethindrone/EE 1/20 daily, multivitamin daily, TPN nightly, vedolizumab 300 IV q8wk (GI infusion center).
Allergies: NSAIDs (GI intolerance, ineffective); gabapentin (ineffective).
FH: mother — depression, type 2 diabetes. Father — Crohn's. Sister — anxiety; sister is her main support. Maternal aunt — DVT.
SH: On disability leave, used to be an administrative assistant. Lives alone in an apartment in Florence. Smokes lightly, about a pack a week. Drinks socially, a cocktail or two on weekends. No drugs.

ROS: as above; no fevers, no abdominal pain beyond baseline, no line problems.

Exam: thin, tired-appearing, cooperative, affect flat. HEENT unremarkable. Neck supple, no thyromegaly. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender, well-healed midline and prior surgical scars. Right chest tunneled catheter, dressing clean and dry, no erythema or tenderness at exit site. No edema. Neuro grossly nonfocal.
PHQ-9 21. GAD-7 12.

A/P:
1. Recurrent major depression, current episode severe — PHQ-9 21, no SI. Will call her psychiatrist's office today to get her seen sooner. No med changes from me; they manage. Safety plan reviewed, crisis line numbers given.
2. Generalized anxiety — as above. Discussed limiting alprazolam to the prescribed dose.
3. Crohn's / short bowel / TPN — stable per patient, on vedolizumab through GI. Will get GI's latest letter.
4. Low back pain, chronic — no new red flags. Revisit at follow-up.
5. Weight down from 62 kg last fall to 56.9 today — likely mood. Recheck next visit.
6. Health maintenance: baseline CBC, BMP, TSH, lipids, A1c (mom has diabetes). Hep C and HIV screening, she agrees. Pap 2019 normal per old records. Mammogram due — will order at next visit after we sort out mood.
7. Tobacco — advised quitting; not ready yet.

RTC 6-8 weeks.

The hepatitis C and HIV screens were negative. I spoke with your psychiatrist's office; expect a call from them about an earlier appointment. Hang in there and reach out any time.

documents.title: Psychiatry Follow-up
documents.author: psychiatry
documents.body:
OUTPATIENT PSYCHIATRY — FOLLOW-UP
Date of service: 08/24/2020
Patient: Tracy Bianchi, 45-year-old woman

Dear Doctor,

Thank you for your note about Ms. Bianchi. I saw her in follow-up for depressive symptoms that have persisted since about April. She describes four months of constant low mood, loss of pleasure in things she used to enjoy, and trouble holding her concentration. She has lost a meaningful amount of weight, is sleeping poorly, and voices a sense of being worthless.

This is her third major depressive episode; the first came in her late twenties and the second in her mid-thirties, and each needed antidepressant treatment. Her mother has a history of depression. She tells me she is not using any substances.

Current medications: sertraline 100 mg daily, bupropion XL 150 mg daily, alprazolam 0.25 mg as needed (she acknowledges sometimes taking two at night), diphenhydramine 25 mg at bedtime as needed, combined oral contraceptive daily, multivitamin, nightly TPN through her central line, and vedolizumab infusions every 8 weeks through her GI team.
Allergies/intolerances: NSAIDs (ineffective, poor GI tolerance); gabapentin (ineffective).

Mental status: depressed mood and constricted affect; no psychotic features. General physical exam today was unremarkable.
Recent labs from your office (CBC, TSH, basic metabolic panel) are within normal limits.

Impression: Recurrent major depression, current episode severe. Generalized anxiety disorder.

Plan: Continue her current regimen without changes for now. I will see her back in about two months.

Sincerely,
Outpatient Psychiatry

INTESTINAL REHABILITATION / GASTROENTEROLOGY
Visit date: 10/28/2020

Dear Doctor,

Thank you for taking over Ms. Bianchi's primary care. She was seen today for her routine review of home parenteral nutrition.

She has Crohn's disease of the small bowel with short bowel syndrome after several resections and remains dependent on TPN, infused over 12 hours each night through her tunneled central venous catheter. She has had no catheter infections or line malfunctions since her last visit and no Crohn's flares. She continues vedolizumab 300 mg IV every 8 weeks at our infusion center for Crohn's maintenance and tolerates it well. Her weekly home infusion labs have been stable and we made no change to her formula.

Exam: thin, no distress. Abdomen soft and nontender. Catheter exit site clean without erythema.

Plan: continue current TPN prescription and vedolizumab every 8 weeks; weekly labs through home infusion; return in one year or sooner as needed.

Allergies/intolerances: NSAIDs, gabapentin.

Kind regards,
Gastroenterology / Intestinal Rehabilitation

documents.title: After-hours call from sister
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Sister called the after-hours line (pt gave verbal OK, was on the call). This afternoon at the kitchen table Tracy stopped mid-sentence and stared for maybe 45 seconds, wouldn't answer, then was foggy for a few minutes and doesn't remember any of it. No shaking, didn't fall, no incontinence, no injury. Back to herself now, talking normally, no headache, no weakness. No fever. Took no extra pills today per pt.
Told them to call 911 for any repeat episode, shaking, or if she doesn't come back to baseline. No driving. Will see her first thing tomorrow.

documents.title: Acute Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Here with sister re: yesterday's episode (see after-hours note). Sitting at kitchen table, abruptly stopped talking, stared ~45 sec, unresponsive to sister, no recall, confused several minutes after. Sister saw no jerking, she didn't slump or fall. Nothing like it before that either of them knows of. Pt says she's felt "slowed down" and foggy for a while and has trouble concentrating — had blamed the depression. No head injury, no new meds, no alcohol yesterday. Sleep poor as usual.
O: Vitals reviewed, afebrile. Alert, oriented x3, speech fluent, flat. CN II-XII intact, strength 5/5 throughout, sensation intact, reflexes symmetric, finger-nose normal, gait normal. Line site clean.
A/P: Transient episode of unresponsiveness with amnesia and post-event confusion — concerning for a focal seizure. Ddx includes medication effect (alprazolam/diphenhydramine), metabolic.
- CBC, BMP, TSH, B12 today.
- Urgent neurology referral — called; they can see her tomorrow.
- No driving until cleared by neurology. Seizure precautions reviewed (no baths alone, no heights).
- ED if recurs or any convulsion.

documents.title: Neurology Consultation
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
NEUROLOGY CONSULTATION
Date of service: 12/08/2020

Dear Doctor,

Thank you for the same-week referral of Ms. Bianchi, a 45-year-old woman with Crohn's disease and short bowel syndrome on home TPN and recurrent major depression, last seen by her psychiatrist about three months ago.

History: Earlier this week, while seated at her kitchen table, she abruptly stopped speaking and stared ahead for roughly 45 seconds. She did not respond during the spell and has no memory of it; her sister, who witnessed it, says she was muddled for several minutes afterward. Her sister did not see any shaking and she did not lose consciousness or fall. Over recent weeks she has felt mentally "slowed" and has had trouble concentrating, which she had put down to her mood.

Medications: bupropion, sertraline, alprazolam as needed, over-the-counter diphenhydramine at night, oral contraceptive, multivitamin, nightly TPN, vedolizumab infusions every 8 weeks.
Allergies/intolerances: NSAIDs, gabapentin.
Family history: mother with depression and type 2 diabetes; father with Crohn's disease; sister with generalized anxiety (her main support); maternal aunt with DVT.
Social: She reports that she does not drink. She admits that when she cannot sleep she will sometimes take more than one alprazolam.

Examination: vital signs normal. Oriented, with a flat affect; frequent pauses in conversation. Cranial nerves, motor, sensory, reflexes, coordination and gait are normal — no focal findings.
Laboratory (drawn by your office 12/07): CBC, basic metabolic panel, TSH and B12 normal.

Impression: The episode is typical of a focal seizure with impaired awareness arising from the temporal lobe. Diagnosis: temporal lobe epilepsy.

Plan:
1. Start lamotrigine, chosen with her depression in mind and because it does not lower sodium. Titration: 25 mg daily for 2 weeks, 50 mg daily for 2 weeks, 50 mg twice daily for 1 week, 75 mg twice daily for 1 week, then 100 mg twice daily. The target allows for her estrogen-containing contraceptive, which lowers lamotrigine levels. She is to stop it and call us for any rash, and never to stop it suddenly.
2. Routine EEG, scheduled.
3. Seizure precautions and Massachusetts driving restrictions discussed; she understands she should not drive.
4. I will review the EEG and see her back.

Sincerely,
Neurology

medications.sig: Titrate: 25 mg daily for 2 weeks, 50 mg daily for 2 weeks, 50 mg twice daily for 1 week, 75 mg twice daily for 1 week, then 100 mg twice daily

reports.text: Routine awake and drowsy EEG, 21 electrodes, international 10-20 system, with photic stimulation and hyperventilation. Posterior dominant rhythm 9.5 Hz, symmetric and reactive. Intermittent sharp waves over the left temporal region, maximal at T7/F7, seen in wakefulness and drowsiness. No electrographic seizures. Normal response to photic stimulation and hyperventilation.
reports.conclusion: Abnormal EEG: intermittent left temporal sharp waves on a normal background, consistent with a left temporal epileptogenic focus.

documents.title: EEG question
documents.author: patient
documents.body:
Neurology scheduled my EEG for the 22nd. They said come "sleep deprived" — does that mean I should skip my TPN that night? And can I take my alprazolam the night before?
— Tracy

Reply (RN, 12/16): Please run your TPN as usual — it doesn't affect the EEG. Neurology asked for less sleep, not less nutrition. Take your regular medicines unless the neurology office told you otherwise; I left a message with them to confirm about the alprazolam and will call you back.
Addendum (RN, 12/16 15:40): Neurology office says take medications as usual. Patient informed.

Neuro started lamotrigine 12/8 and she followed the titration card — at 100 mg twice daily since yesterday, no rash, a little dizzy the first few days. No further spells since 12/6 per pt and sister. Not driving — sister and a friend are getting her to appointments. Mood "maybe a notch better," still flat in the mornings. Sleep unchanged. TPN without problems.

PHQ-9 15.
Assessment/Plan:
1. Temporal lobe epilepsy — added to problem list. Lamotrigine 100 bid per neuro, no rash. Neuro to follow; she has a f/u with them in March. Precautions reinforced.
2. Recurrent MDD — improving slowly. Psych following.
3. GAD — stable.
4. Weight — holding, slightly up.
5. Short bowel/TPN — CMP and magnesium today for our records (GI gets weekly infusion labs).
Next visit spring; mammogram done in Oct, normal.

documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
NEUROLOGY — RETURN VISIT
Date of service: 03/08/2021

Dear Doctor,

Ms. Bianchi returns after her EEG. The recording showed intermittent left temporal sharp waves over a normal background, which supports the diagnosis of left temporal lobe epilepsy. She and her sister report no further events since the episode in December.

She completed the lamotrigine titration and has taken 100 mg twice daily since 01/19 without rash or other side effects. Given her short bowel we checked a trough level today to confirm absorption: 4.8 mcg/mL (reference 2.5-15.0), in range.

Neurologic examination remains normal.

Continue lamotrigine 100 mg twice daily; refills from our office. We reviewed seizure precautions again. She will continue to hold off on driving until she has been event-free for the required interval. She knows to call us with any further spells.

Follow-up in neurology in one year, or sooner as needed.

Sincerely,
Neurology

documents.title: Office Visit — back pain
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
CC: back pain

Low back pain much worse the last few weeks, "unbearable" some days, across the low back, no radiation down the legs. No numbness, no weakness, no bowel/bladder change from her baseline, no fever, no trauma. Has tried "everything" — NSAIDs and gabapentin in the past did nothing, PT did nothing. Heat helps a little. Tearful talking about it, feels nobody can fix it.
Quit smoking ~2 months ago, about a pack a week before. Proud of that.
COVID vaccines at the pharmacy 3/23 and 4/13 — recorded.

Exam: uncomfortable changing position. Tender over lumbar paraspinals bilaterally, no midline bony tenderness. SLR negative bilaterally. Strength 5/5 LE, sensation intact, reflexes symmetric. Gait normal.
Pain 8/10. PHQ-9 17.

A/P
# Chronic low back pain, flare — mechanical by exam, no red flags. Labs to make sure we're not missing inflammation/thyroid/vit D: CBC, ESR, TSH, 25-OH D. Referral to pain management; she's open to it. Heat, gentle stretching.
# Recurrent MDD — worse with the pain. Letting psych know.
# Tobacco — quit ~Feb 2021, congratulated.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Tracy — your blood count is normal, the inflammation marker (ESR) is 20, thyroid 2.5 and vitamin D 30, all in the normal range. Nothing here explains the back pain flare, which fits with a muscular/mechanical cause. Pain management will call you to schedule.

documents.title: Pain Management Consultation
documents.author: pain management
documents.body:
INTERVENTIONAL PAIN MANAGEMENT — NEW CONSULTATION
Date of service: 05/10/2021

Referring: Primary care
Reason: worsening low back pain

Ms. Bianchi is a 46-year-old woman with Crohn's disease, short bowel syndrome and home TPN, who was seen by psychiatry last August and by neurology in December. She comes in for low back pain that has escalated to the point she calls it unbearable. In her words she has tried "everything": NSAIDs and a gabapentin trial gave no meaningful relief, and she describes an earlier course of physical therapy as "useless." She feels hopeless that it will ever get better. She was tearful through much of the visit and said more than once that no one is able to help her.

Medications: sertraline 100 mg daily; bupropion XL 150 mg daily; alprazolam 0.25 mg as needed (at times two at night); diphenhydramine 25 mg at night as needed; combined oral contraceptive; lamotrigine 100 mg twice daily; multivitamin; nightly TPN via central line; vedolizumab IV every 8 weeks.
Allergies/intolerances: NSAIDs (ineffective, poor GI tolerance); gabapentin (ineffective).
Social: former light smoker, stopped about three months ago (had been about one pack a week); social drinker, one to two cocktails on weekends; on disability leave, previously an administrative assistant.
Family: mother — depression, type 2 diabetes; father — Crohn's; sister — anxiety; maternal aunt — DVT.

Exam: tenderness to palpation of the lumbar paraspinal muscles. Neurologic examination of the lower extremities is normal — no motor, sensory or reflex deficit.
Labs drawn by primary care 04/20/2021: CBC normal, ESR of 20 mm/hr, vitamin D 30 ng/mL, TSH 2.5 mIU/L.

Assessment: Chronic mechanical low back pain without radiculopathy. I do not see a target for an injection or other procedure.

Recommendations:
1. Daily home exercise and staying active; I gave her a written core and hip program.
2. Her mood is clearly tied up with her pain; please continue to coordinate with her psychiatrist.
3. No medication changes from our side.
4. Follow up with us as needed.

Thank you for the referral.
Pain Management

Plan: no changes. Return in three months.

Outpatient Psychiatry

Meds: sertraline 100, bupropion XL 150, alprazolam 0.25 prn, diphenhydramine 25 qhs prn, lamotrigine 100 bid, norethindrone/EE 1/20, MVI, TPN, vedolizumab q8wk (GI).
Allergies: NSAIDs (GI intolerance, ineffective); gabapentin (ineffective).

ROS negative except back pain and low mood.

Exam: Well-appearing, thin. Weight 59.7. HEENT normal, TMs clear. Neck without nodes or thyroid enlargement. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Breasts deferred to imaging per pt preference. Abdomen soft, nontender, healed scars. Tunneled line R chest, site clean. Back: paraspinal tenderness, full strength. Skin no rashes. Mood fair, affect more reactive than last year.

Plan:
- Tdap today (no record of one in prior chart).
- Mammogram — order placed for the fall.

RTC 3 months.

documents.title: Orthopedic Consultation
documents.author: orthopedics
documents.body:
ORTHOPAEDIC SURGERY — HIP CLINIC
New consultation, 10/25/2021

Dear Doctor,

Thank you for asking us to see Ms. Bianchi, who has chronic mechanical low back pain followed by pain management (seen there in May). For about six months she has found walking harder, and she feels unsteady whenever her weight is on the right leg. Climbing stairs, the right hip tends to buckle.

Medications and allergies reviewed (intolerances: NSAIDs, gabapentin).
Social: former light smoker, social alcohol, on disability leave.

Examination: She walks with a mild limp. Asked to balance on the right leg alone, the pelvis sags on the opposite (left) side below level — a positive Trendelenburg sign on the right. Right hip abduction is weak on manual testing. Sensation is intact throughout and reflexes are preserved. Hip range of motion is full without pain.

Impression: Right hip abductor weakness with a Trendelenburg gait, in keeping with right superior gluteal nerve palsy.

Plan:
- Physical therapy for hip abductor (gluteus medius/minimus) strengthening and gait training; referral sent from our office.
- Return to clinic as needed if she is not improving.

Thank you,
Orthopaedic Surgery
